column2: Nym takes your hand and turns it over, as if to read it. “This is the third time you've come. The other two times you had another name.” She looks up at you. “Don't worry. I've had many too.”
The valley has rewound itself. But those who remember remember more than before.
New faces in this Cycle
Recruitable companion
📜 Will join you through their own story
Teodora
Gravedigger of the Silent
She has dug graves for forty years. She says she has already buried you once. She isn't joking.
She carries a shovel on her back and the names of the dead by heart.
Mother Bones
Witch of the Swamps
She lives in a hut of roots on the edge of the Swamps. She talks to the trees, and the trees answer.
Ilyas
The refugee who remembers
In every Cycle someone sells him, saves him or forgets him. He, instead, remembers everything.
The Voice in the Well
Something beneath Hondovalle
The well above which the portal opens. For a few Cycles now, at night, it has been calling bearers by name.
The Bearer's Tomb
Teodora says the bearer of the previous Cycle does not rest. Their echo wanders the Cemetery of the Betrayed, beyond the fourth floor.
You met the echo of the one who carried the Burden before you. Go back to Teodora.
The bearer who came before has found their place.
The Pact of Roots
Mother Bones wants 80 wood for her hut, and wants you to go down to the fifth floor of the Swamps, where the heart of the swamp still beats.
You have seen the heart of the swamp. Go back to Mother Bones.
The Pact of Roots has been decided.
The Sewn Eye
Ilyas says the Market Shadows set fire to Hondovalle in every Cycle. Ask Varo about the sewn eye.
Varo spoke of a room at the top of the Tower of Silence, where the sewn eye keeps the register of the Cycles. Reach the fifth floor of the Tower.
You found the Register of Cycles. Go back to Ilyas.
You know who burns the valley in every Cycle, and why.
Gravedigger
She buries the dead and, when needed, wakes them. She joins you after The Bearer's Tomb.
Tarn
Deserter of the Cult
He wore chains for the Cult. Now he wears them to remember never to go back. You'll find him in the Swamps.
Seer refugee
He has seen the valley burn too many times to still be afraid. He joins you after The Sewn Eye.

An old woman cleans a shovel as if it were a sword. She looks at you for a long time. “I know you. No, not you. The one before you. {legacy}. I buried them myself, in my own way.” She leans on the handle. “Only they didn't stay buried.”
How can you remember? No one remembers the previous Cycle.
What do you mean they didn't stay buried?
Listen to the sound of the shovel. Watch her.

“The Silent Gravediggers don't forget. It is our vow. When Krak rewinds the valley, we keep the names.” She touches a nameless gravestone. “This one is theirs. I've carved the name three times. Every morning it's smooth again.”
What do they want from me?
Her hands have shovel calluses and chain scars. She isn't just a gravedigger: she was a Warden of the Valley. And she is afraid, but not of you. Of what lies beneath the Cemetery.
You were a Warden. What lies beneath the Cemetery?

“Their echo wanders beyond the fourth floor of the Cemetery of the Betrayed. Whoever dies carrying the Burden goes nowhere: they stay there, and wait for the next one.” She puts the shovel in your hands for a moment, then takes it back. “They're waiting for you. Go tell them they can stop.”
I'll go. I owe them that.
Why should I help a dead person?
“Because one day the dead one will be you.” She says it without malice, the way one says it will rain. “And you'll want someone to come and tell you.”
…All right. I'll go.
“They're still down there. I feel it when I dig: the Cemetery earth is colder where they pass.”

Teodora listens to your story without interrupting. When you finish, she goes to the smooth gravestone and runs her palm over it. The name {legacy} resurfaces, carved, as if it had always been there. “Good,” is all she says. Then she shoulders her shovel. “I've settled the dead. Now it's the turn of the living. I'm coming with you.”
Welcome, Teodora.
Teodora joins your party.
The party is full of people who will die. Are you sure?
She laughs, a dry sound like falling earth. “Kid, I already know where I'll put them.”
Then come.
Teodora digs. She doesn't look up. “Still alive? Good. Come back when you're not.”
By the fire, Teodora takes off her boots and counts names on her fingers. When she reaches the tenth she stops. “This was my son. A Warden too. In the Cycle he died, the bearer chose the Cult.”
I'm sorry.
Which bearer? Me?
“Don't be sorry. Remember him. That's different.”
I'll remember him.
She looks at you for a long time. “No. One before you. But you had the same eyes when you arrived.”
Teodora sharpens her shovel. “Tomorrow we go down. Tomorrow I bury someone.”

The hut is made of living roots that breathe. Inside, a woman with fingers long as branches braids human hair into a crown. “Third Cycle, eh? It shows. In the first you laugh, in the second you cry, in the third you start listening.”
You know about the Cycles?
Whose hair is that?
The roots are moving. Find out what they are.

“The trees know. Roots don't rewind: they grow beneath Krak, through the Cycles, and each time they tighten a little more around its Heart.” She smiles, green-toothed. “One day they'll strangle it. If someone helps them.”
How can I help them?
“Bearers like you. One per Cycle. They leave it to me as payment.” She strokes a lock. “This one was {legacy}'s. Lovely hair, terrible ideas.”
What do you want from me, then?
They aren't tree roots. They are veins. Veins of Krak, petrified and covered in moss, that the witch has bent the way you bend a dog. You are looking at a piece of the Heart, tamed.
You tamed a piece of Krak?

“Bring me eighty wood: the hut must grow. And go down to the fifth floor of the Swamps. There lies the heart of the swamp, a piece of Krak that still beats. You decide what to do with it. I only want to know what you'll choose.”
And what's in it for me?
“A crown.” She shows you the one of hair. “Not this one. A better one. Made of what you'll find down there.”
All right.
“Eighty wood, and the heart of the swamp. The roots are waiting. They are patient: I'm less so.”
Here's the wood.
The roots stretch out, take the wood and swallow it. The hut grows a room before your eyes. “Good guest. Now the heart.”

Mother Bones listens, her fingers still on the crown. “You saw the heart and came back. Not everyone comes back.” She stands. “Now decide. My roots can squeeze that heart until it goes silent, but it will take time and someone to feed them. Or you can take its heartbeat for yourself.”
Feed the roots. Let them strangle Krak, one Cycle at a time.
The roots of Mother Bones squeeze the Heart of Krak.
Give me the heartbeat. I'll carry it.
You took the heartbeat of the swamp.
Neither. The heart stays where it is.
The heart of the swamp still beats, untouched.
Mother Bones braids. “The roots say hello. I don't.”

A thin boy, with eyes too old for his face, waits for you outside the inn. “Ilyas,” he says, before you can ask. “The refugee. The one you sell, save or forget. What will you do in this Cycle, {name}? No, don't answer. You'll tell me anyway.”
You remember the Cycles?
I won't sell you.
What do you want?
“All of them. Four times I've seen the valley burn. Four times the same figure with an eye sewn on its cloak, walking away through the flames before the portal opens.”
The Market Shadows.
He laughs, without joy. “The others said that too. {legacy} said it with a hand on their heart.” Then he grows serious. “I don't want promises. I want a truth.”
What truth?

“Who sets the fire, every time. And why the fire comes before the portal, not after. Ask Varo about the sewn eye: it's their seal, and he lies better than anyone, which means he knows more than anyone.”
I'll find out.
I have no time for the ghosts of the Cycles.
“The fire comes before the portal,” Ilyas repeats, like a prayer. “Remember that. It's the only thing that matters.”

You show him the pages of the Register of Cycles. Ilyas reads them in silence, one by one, until he finds his own name. Beside it, in every Cycle, the same kind of word: “sold”, “saved”, “forgotten”. He closes the book. “The Shadows don't burn the valley for Krak. They burn it because every Cycle the price of memories goes up.” He looks at you. “This time, I want to choose what they write next to my name.”
Then write it walking with me.
Ilyas joins your party.
I'll sell the Register to the Shadows. They'll pay any price.
You sold the Register of Cycles to the Shadows.
Ilyas looks at the well. “Every Cycle it's a little deeper. Have you noticed?”

At night you lean over the well. From the black water rises your own voice, but older. “{name}. Cycle {cycle}. You came back again.” A long pause. “Every time you start over, I become a little more awake. You know that, don't you?”
Then I'll stop coming back.
What do you want in exchange for a gift?
“I am what remains when the valley rewinds. The choices no one remembers end up here, at the bottom. I am made of all your choices, {name}. Of all your Cycles.”
Then give me something of mine.
The voice laughs, and the water trembles. “No. You won't stop. No one stops. That's what feeds me.”
Then give me something for the road.
“I can give back a piece of what you lost in the previous Cycles. Choose which.”
Strength: give me back the relics I've spent.
Memory: let me remember the map.
Peace: take some of my Burden.
Nothing. I take nothing from you.
Silence. Then, softly: “Interesting. No one had ever refused.” The water goes still. You feel you've done something Krak did not expect.
The well is silent. But you feel it is listening.

Orsola freezes with the mug in mid-air. “Strange. I dreamed of someone like you, dead on my floor. Their name was {legacy}.” She shakes her head. “Dreams, in Hondovalle, are sometimes memories that arrive late.”
Tell me about the dream.
It was a dream. Nothing more.

“It was raining ash. I closed your… their eyes. Before dying they said: ‘tell the next one not to trust the well’.” She dries her hands, for too long. “There. I said it. Now don't ask me anything else.”
Thank you, Orsola.
How many Cycles have you seen, Nym?
She counts on her fingers. Runs out of fingers. Starts again. “More than you can count. But fewer than Krak counts.”

Varo stops smiling when you mention the sewn eye. “The boy sent you to me. Naturally.” He looks around. “Not here. At the top of the Tower of Silence, on the fifth floor, is the room where the Shadows keep the Register of Cycles. What you'll find there is none of my business.”
Why are you telling me?
Thank you, Varo.
“Because my name is in that register too. And I don't like the word next to it.” He puts his hat back on. “Go, before I change my mind.”
The Echo of the One Before
Among the gravestones, a figure with your same Burden on its shoulders. The face is blurred, like a worn coin. “Are you the next one?” says the echo of {legacy}. “Then you already know how it ends.”
Listen to their last wish.
The echo whispers where they hid their last relic. Then it smiles, relieved, and begins to fade. “Do better than me.”
Take their weapon. They don't need it anymore.
The blade is cold and heavy with memories. The echo watches you take it, without anger. “I took it from someone too.”
Tell them they can stop waiting.
The echo closes its eyes. For the first time in a whole Cycle, it sits down. Then it is gone.
The Heart of the Swamp
Beneath the red water, a heart as big as a barrel beats slowly. The roots of Mother Bones surround it, but don't touch it. They are waiting for you.
Touch it to feel what it dreams.
The heart dreams of a valley without bearers. It is the saddest dream you have ever felt.
Mark it for the roots, without touching it.
You tie a blade of grass around a root. The roots shiver. They understood.
The Prisoner in Chains

A huge man, chained to a post in the mud, the Cult's symbol burned on his chest and then scratched out with a knife. “My name is Tarn. I deserted. Leave me here and the Cult will come back for me tonight.”
Break the chains. Come with me.
The chains fall. Tarn rises, taller than you thought. “I owe you a life. I always pay my lives back.” Tarn joins you.
Hand him over to Vesper.
Tarn doesn't scream when they take him away. He only looks at you, the way you look at someone you've already seen die.
Leave him where he is.
You walk away. Behind you, Tarn starts pulling at the chains again, calmly, as he has done for days.
The Register of Cycles

A circular room, without windows. On a lectern, an enormous book with an eye sewn on the cover. Every page is a Cycle. Every line is a choice. You find {legacy}'s page. Then you find yours, already begun.
Tear out the pages and bring them to Ilyas.
The pages tear with a sound of bones. Somewhere in the Tower, someone screams.
Read your page to the end.
The last line of your page is still empty. Beside it, in pencil, someone has written: “we'll see”.
Hondovalle Is No Longer the Same

The village stands again, as if nothing had happened. But something is different: the inn has one more window, the Cemetery gravestones are turned toward the well, and someone has carved a name on the square's wall. {legacy}.
Leave the name where it is.
The name stays. Now and then, passing by, someone lays a flower on it.
Erase it. This Cycle is mine.
You scrape the letters away with your knife. At night, you dream of someone asking you why.
“I've dug enough graves. Not mine.”
“Too many names… too many.”
“Tonight I bury no one.”
“Get up. I'm not done with you.”
“The chains… I still feel them.”
“The Cult was right about me.”
“Never on my knees again.”
“Come and get me, now!”
“Four Cycles. Always the same ending.”
“Sell me and be done with it.”
“This time I write my own line.”
“I remember everything. Even how to win.”
Teodora turns the gift over, sniffs it, puts it in her pocket. “No one has given me anything since my son died. All right. I'll keep it for when someone needs it.”
Teodora takes you to a corner of the Cemetery and shows you a smooth gravestone. “This one is for you. I won't write anything on it. It's a promise I won't use it.” (Teodora gains less Strain.)
Teodora carves your name on her shovel's handle, next to her son's. “So if Krak rewinds everything, at least here you'll stay.” (Teodora +10% health and attack.)
Tarn looks at the gift as if it were a trap. Then he squeezes it so hard his knuckles go white. “In the Cult they only gave us orders.”
Tarn shows you the scars on his chest, one for every rite he obeyed. “I count them every night. Since you came, I count faster.” (Tarn gains less Strain.)
Tarn melts the last link of his chains and makes a medal with your name. “Now the chains are mine. And I wear them for you.” (Tarn +10% health and attack.)
Ilyas smiles, surprised. “In four Cycles no one has ever given me anything. They bought me, sold me, saved me. Never gave.”
Ilyas tells you how {legacy} dies, in his Cycle. Then he tells you how to avoid it. “I'm telling you because this time I want to see you reach the end.” (Ilyas gains less Strain.)
Ilyas writes your name on his arm, with the Register's ink. “So next Cycle, if it starts again, I'll recognize you first.” (Ilyas +10% health and attack.)
🤝 {c} joins you.
{c} has joined your party.
